destinations.title: What would detecting primordial CMB tensors imply for string inflation, moduli stabilization, and the gravitino mass, particularly in models based on the simplest KKLT construction?
Are omitted bulk and localized terms suppressed in hierarchical LVS, and can BPS charge–tension matching forbid candidate induced potentials?
Which intersection structures admit the ordinary LVS hierarchy without forcing another physical cycle below the string scale?
Does the conjectured KK correction spoil stabilization and the gaugino hierarchy in the explicit two-modulus large-volume model?
Can one bulk divisor become exponentially larger than another while physical cycles remain controlled and the scalar potential stabilizes both directions?
Can calculations or symmetries exclude mixed-cycle and higher-loop terms that are less suppressed than the retained α′ effect?
Can loops replace the usual negative-Euler-characteristic requirement or improve purely perturbative Kähler stabilization?
Are selected string-loop corrections compatible with stabilization and soft supersymmetry breaking in an assumed type-IIB large-volume vacuum?
Do string loop corrections from D-branes and O-planes invalidate large-volume stabilization or its soft supersymmetry-breaking predictions, particularly the suppressed gaugino masses?
How must compactification radius, string length, and string coupling vary when lower-dimensional gravitational strength is held fixed?

Can the maximal-supergravity multiplet be isolated from string theory while gravitational interactions remain at finite strength? The question requires examining additional nonperturbative states as well as perturbative string excitations.
Determine whether Quintom matter can support a nonzero minimum scale factor in Einstein gravity and then evolve above w = -1, allowing a possible connection to conventional expanding cosmology.
Can a low-energy Abelian gauge symmetry protect the proton without obstructing fermion masses or a neutrino seesaw? The proposed symmetry must also be family universal and anomaly free.

Can the extra proton-protecting U(1) coexist with light active neutrinos? The neutral singlets and heavy-singlet Higgs VEV provide operators that preserve the residual gauge symmetry while generating a seesaw mass matrix.

The construction supplies string-derived matter charges for testing whether proton protection and realistic fermion masses can coexist. Its three twisted generations each couple to a different world-sheet U(1) current.

The effective model tests whether the string-inspired charge pattern can combine a high seesaw-breaking scale with a lower proton-protecting gauge symmetry and phenomenologically relevant lepton-number violation.

Does an asymptotic bubble observer evade every finite-entropy observational restriction? The apparent infinity of collision observations exposes a gap between the demonstrated rolling-inflation bound and a proposed universal limit on information about de Sitter space.

Can a flat-space observer inside a bubble use collisions to obtain information about an eternally inflating parent vacuum? This setting removes the classically rolling adiabatic clock on which the main non-eternal-inflation bound was built.

How does a future observer recover information from inflationary fluctuations? A local clock shift changes the end-of-inflation hypersurface, and its curvature becomes a density perturbation when the wavelength re-enters the horizon.

Does gauge invariance itself prevent local observables and time evolution? Introducing coordinate fields in nondynamical flat geometry shows that the relevant obstruction is dynamical gravity, which makes causal separation fluctuate and requires physical clocks.

Can low-curvature Hamiltonian evolution on nice slices describe an entire unitary evaporation? The reviewed paradox contrasts the entropy increase predicted by independent interior and exterior degrees of freedom with the shrinking information capacity assigned to the hole.

Which NEC violations threaten the measurement and entropy arguments? The paper singles out stable propagating clock sectors that can approach non-gravitation, distinguishing them from quantum effects and projected objects that do not provide the same measuring apparatus.

How can a finite de Sitter entropy constrain observations when an inflationary region expands into many causally separated Hubble volumes? Ending inflation in a suitable FRW universe turns inaccessible early fluctuations into density modes that can later be observed.

A finite inflationary episode provides an observable regulator of de Sitter space: modes leave the early Hubble horizon and can subsequently re-enter a decelerating universe. The relevant entropy changes with H and is evaluated at the end when bounding the total duration.

The proposed extension seeks Higgs-mass stabilization by adding higher derivative kinetic operators throughout the Standard Model. Each operator introduces a massive resonance rather than a new stable asymptotic particle, with its mass initially independent of the masses in other representations.

The hierarchy problem asks why the Higgs mass remains small compared with a very high ultraviolet scale. This paper investigates whether higher derivative kinetic operators and their massive Lee-Wick resonances can remove quadratic radiative sensitivity while retaining a usable perturbative theory.
Can a symmetry-motivated scalar provide temporary acceleration with better radiative stability than an arbitrary low-energy potential?
Which kinds of scalar motion can yield acceleration, reduce sensitivity to initial conditions, or terminate an accelerating epoch?
Can measurements of cosmic expansion and structure growth reveal whether acceleration arises from a cosmological constant, an evolving scalar field, or modified gravitational physics?
How does a smooth canonical scalar field produce a time-dependent negative pressure and affect cosmic expansion?
What must an experiment measure beyond a nearly cosmological-constant average equation of state?

Can observing red discriminate an all-red universe from a universe containing both red and blue cycles when observers may occur in many cycles? The model isolates the role of observer abundance without specifying real cosmological dynamics.

What information must a candidate physical theory contain before observational evidence can discriminate it from alternatives? The framework requires a specified prior, a physical description of the data, and calculable observation likelihoods for each candidate.

Should a theory predicting many intelligent jovians be penalized because humans would be a minority? The example isolates that question by specifying an observed human count while leaving the jovian population unmeasured.

What is observed when a large universe contains several regions with exactly the same records? The paper treats the known information as the occurrence of at least one matching region, while leaving its global location and unobserved origin unspecified.

Can the abundance of observers unlike humans invalidate a cosmological theory even when the theory predicts the observations humans actually possess? The answer depends on the comparison class, the observation event, and whether a physical sampling protocol or an explicit prior preference is supplied.

What warrants a typicality assumption: observed populations, a conjectured prediction, or preference? The source separates these grounds and emphasizes that choosing a class already affects whether humans appear typical.

How should one ask what observers could have measured if a now-known quantity had been unknown? The paper requires a physical specification of which records may vary and which features continue to identify the conditioning system.
The breaking mechanism is a mismatch between the N=1 supersymmetry selected by the compact orientifold and the N=1 supersymmetry locally preserved by negative conifold flux.
Does the supergravity Kähler correction persist in the small-gs|N| antibrane gauge theory, where the microscopic coupling to the misaligned supergravity algebra is unresolved?
Which gauge theory coupled to N=1 supergravity reproduces the negative-flux throat whose locally preserved supersymmetry is misaligned with the compact orientifold?
Can warping turn the high energy associated with an antibrane flux dual into a hierarchically small supersymmetry-breaking scale while maintaining a controlled, stabilized compactification?

Can all subsystem entropies of one holographic state determine its classical bulk geometry? The proposed advantage over null-endpoint data is sensitivity to the metric's conformal factor and access to deeper bulk regions.
How can the entanglement entropy of a boundary region be represented geometrically when the dual bulk evolves in time and supplies no preferred spatial slice?

Does classical positive null energy suffice to make holographic subsystem entropy increase throughout a general gravitational collapse, and does that behavior survive Hawking-radiation corrections? The source proposes the broader behavior without supplying a general proof.

How does the entanglement entropy of a fixed-width boundary interval respond to homogeneous gravitational collapse? A prescribed null-time-dependent Vaidya mass permits this question without requiring an explicit field-theory construction of the evolving state.

How can two boundary CFTs that appear dynamically decoupled exhibit correlations computed through a connected Euclidean bulk? The wormhole example tests whether a correlated or entangled joint state can account for the bulk prediction.

What interval-like entanglement growth is induced by a bubble geometry whose boundary spatial sphere changes size? The calculation must distinguish a fixed global-AdS-time subsystem from one at fixed de Sitter time.
Can a boundary entropy bound in a cutoff QFT with induced gravity motivate a covariant bulk representation of entanglement?
Can entanglement between otherwise noninteracting boundary theories explain nonzero correlations associated with a connected multiple-boundary bulk wormhole?

Does the covariant entropy prescription reproduce the interval entropy of a stationary CFT state carrying momentum? Rotating BTZ tests this question because a preferred constant-time bulk slice need not contain the relevant extremal geodesic.
How much additional hemispherical entanglement is associated with a static excited boundary state represented by a bulk radiation star?
Does the proposed covariant entropy increase as a collapsing bulk black hole represents thermalization of a boundary state?

How does a finite warped compactification restrict the radial range of a brane inflaton? The relevant geometric input is the throat contribution to the full volume that determines the reduced Planck mass.

Can the tensor and scalar predictions of DBI inflation satisfy compactification geometry and cosmological observations simultaneously, with constraints insensitive to the detailed potential and throat profile?

Can additional non-Abelian brane degrees of freedom enlarge the effective inflationary field excursion while preserving a small geometric radial range? The proposed model uses coincident branes and a fuzzy-sphere factor W.
Can fluxless M-theory stabilization by a racetrack and hidden meson yield a de Sitter vacuum with a sufficiently broad geometric decompactification barrier?
Can perturbative corrections alone stabilize a volume modulus and leave a broad decompactification barrier after a consistent uplift?
How long does an uplifted string/M-theory de Sitter vacuum survive against tunneling toward infinite-volume decompactification when no additional local minimum remains after uplift?
Does a nonsupersymmetric AdS vacuum at exponentially large compactification volume retain a sufficiently broad decompactification barrier after uplift?
Does uplifting a nonperturbatively stabilized type-IIB AdS vacuum leave a sufficiently broad barrier against volume decompactification?

Does the slowest normalized damping approach the threshold along some near-extremal sequence, so that limsup R_S = 1? The paper's upper comparisons do not supply the lower information needed to decide this equality.

Does temperature impose a universal lower limit on relaxation time, and do near-extreme black holes attain its coefficient? The rate entering this question is the slowest relaxation rate of the system.

How do fundamental Kerr quasinormal frequencies behave as rotation approaches its maximal value? The analysis uses the positive near-extremal parameter σ and studies the limit from subextreme black holes.

Which decay rate belongs in a bound on the relaxation of the whole system? The relevant quantity is the slowest admitted rate, which can differ from either of the particular fundamental modes previously examined.
How much entanglement can occur across a cut in the unique ground state of a finite one-dimensional chain when interaction range, interaction strength, and the excitation gap are controlled?

Can string physics become important before curvature or blueshift effects become uncontrollable? A slowly contracting circle with antiperiodic fermions reaches a winding-tachyon instability at string size while the singularity remains parametrically far away in time.

How can a locally flat quotient model a big crunch, big bang and chronology violation? Misner space identifies points by a discrete boost, producing shrinking spatial circles in two wedges and compact timelike circles in the other two.

Can a spacetime big bang be described by gauge degrees of freedom that become tractable when the string geometry fails? The reviewed null linear-dilaton construction exchanges early strong string coupling for weak worldvolume Yang–Mills coupling.

What is the simplest homogeneous approach to a spacelike singularity? Vacuum Kasner evolution gives anisotropic power-law contraction, constrained so that a generic solution has one growing and two shrinking scale factors toward t=0.

Does eliminating quotient fixed points eliminate causal pathology? Grant space shows that a smooth quotient can still contain CTCs, including curves through regions where the identification generator itself is spacelike.

Can a supersymmetric Lorentz quotient still exhibit a collapsing circle? The parabolic quotient produces a pinching geometry in which lightcone time also controls the circle radius, giving a null crunch followed by a bang.

Can a black-hole interior isolate the effects of a spacelike singularity from strong local curvature? The BTZ quotient supplies such a laboratory because its local curvature is inherited from AdS3, while its global geometry has a horizon and singularity.

What replaces the classical description of a spacelike singularity in string theory, and can the associated divergences or closed timelike curves be controlled? The review compares several partial approaches without asserting a complete resolution.
Can canonical Kerr black holes analytically attain the proposed universal relaxation bound τ ≥ ℏ/(πT) in the extremal limit, using perturbations with large azimuthal number?

How do non-holomorphic string thresholds and instanton correlation functions determine holomorphic Wilsonian couplings, constrain matter Kähler metrics, and generate perturbative or instanton corrections to Fayet-Iliopoulos terms?

Can the axion and dilaton fields of a string compactification support a smooth Euclidean throat? The relevant classical equations use an indefinite scalar metric obtained by continuing the axionic variables while retaining ordinary dilaton kinetic signs.

What selects contributing Euclidean gravitational saddles when smooth low-energy solutions appear incompatible with the expected boundary correlators? The paper leaves open topology exclusion, contour exclusion and alternative observables.
The AdS3 × S3 × T4 background supplies a known holographic laboratory in which a small, regular string wormhole could be tested against the properties of an ordinary finite-charge quantum system.

Can a nonsingular Euclidean wormhole in a string background with a known CFT dual induce intrinsic randomness in couplings, even after the fundamental theory and vacuum are fixed? The proposed test requires localized wormhole ends that preserve the original boundary conditions.
Can infrared brane supersymmetry breaking generate viable ultraviolet visible soft terms when gauge-coupling moduli were first stabilized supersymmetrically by nonperturbative dynamics?
How do stabilization and localization determine the relative strengths of modulus and supergravity transmission of supersymmetry breaking, and therefore the visible soft masses?
Could superparticle masses reconstructed from gluino and squark cascades distinguish the conditional mirage-mediation pattern?
Which generalized NS-NS flux configurations admit consistent four-dimensional IIA orientifold descriptions and useful moduli potentials?

Which combinations of H, metric, Q, and R flux admit consistent four-dimensional N=1 IIA orientifold descriptions, how do they generate D-terms and stabilize moduli, and which admit ten-dimensional constructions with correct flux quantization?
How far can duality twists extend across string theories, fiber geometries, and twisted sectors while retaining controlled low-energy physics?
What is the R-R charge lattice when NS-NS coefficients are logarithms of integral monodromies rather than integer inherited-form coefficients?
Which effective generalized-flux configurations have ten-dimensional origins, and can all their constraints be formulated using orientifold cohomology?
This model supplies an explicit stabilized vacuum in which modulus masses and interactions can be calculated rather than assigned generic gravitational strengths.

Which microscopic cycle controls observable interactions, and how do matter wave functions depend on the compactification moduli? These assumptions determine whether canonical mass eigenstates couple at the string or Planck scale.

Can primordial inflation produce the observed perturbations while ending in an intermediate-string-scale vacuum with low-energy supersymmetry? The paper assumes an answer exists and restricts its calculations to subsequent evolution.
Can a second photon line, cosmological energy injection or low-energy matter interactions test the long-lived MeV scalar? These are proposed extensions of the explicit photon and electron analysis.

How does an explicitly stabilized modulus sector change reheating, relic abundance and decay signals? The paper tests whether large-volume compactifications evade problems inferred from generic gravitationally coupled scalars.

What photon signal follows if a surviving light modulus is a subcomponent of Galactic and cosmological dark matter? The abundance and spatial distribution are phenomenological inputs rather than outputs of the proposed early-universe dilution.

Which cosmological problems persist when moduli are heavy, and which depend on assumptions about their decay products or mediation mechanism? The review separates early decay from safe gravitino production, dark-matter abundance and vacuum stability.

Can explicitly computed interactions between a mobile D3-brane and moduli-stabilizing wrapped branes be fine-tuned to permit slow-roll warped brane inflation, while keeping the inflationary region inside a geometrically controlled throat?

Can D7-embedding-dependent threshold corrections cancel moduli-stabilization forces on a mobile D3-brane sufficiently to realize inflation driven by D3–anti-D3 Coulomb attraction? If cancellation is only local, can inflation occur and can the brane reach the tip?
How does uplift energy move the KKLT volume minimum? The tip potential provides a supersymmetric AdS reference, its depth and an inverse-square positive contribution.

How can D3 motion, warped geometry and nonperturbative volume stabilization share a four-dimensional Einstein-frame description? A fiducial metric fixes the reference throat, while the breathing mode records the volume response to brane displacement.

The mobile D3 position provides the inflaton candidate in a warped throat. Warping suppresses the anti-D3 energy, while conifold geometry supplies calculable radial and angular dependence for forces induced by moduli stabilization.

Can induced D7 magnetic fields change the D3 potential or its nonperturbative gauge-coupling dependence? The calculation combines a supersymmetric holomorphic D7 with a leading warp-factor perturbation.

Can a simple symmetric wrapped-brane embedding yield a stable radial path with locally small inflaton curvature? The Kuperstein cycle supplies an explicit holomorphic prefactor and a residual SO(3) symmetry.

Can a mobile D3-brane inflate after volume stabilization, wrapped-brane forces and geometric parameter correlations are included? The target is a construction derived from compactification data, with sufficient control to assess inflation and its predictions.

This construction removes Kähler moduli so that a type IIB flux superpotential can involve every surviving geometric modulus and the axio-dilaton. It supplies a setting in which flux stabilization can be studied without adding the usual Kähler-modulus superpotential terms.

Can increasing quantized flux produce controlled supersymmetric vacua with a mass gap between every modulus and the AdS curvature scale? The paper tests whether the flux freedom that controls an expansion also forces some scalar Compton wavelengths to remain comparable to the AdS radius.

Do anisotropic bulk solutions obey the same mass scaling, and can strong-coupling flux vacua be described by a tractable dual gauge theory? A separate unresolved task is to compute the correction coefficients that decide whether the proposed stabilization and uplift mechanisms work.

Does a real function of the moduli generate non-BPS extremal black-hole evolution and its attractor endpoints? The paper also asks how far such a description can survive when the non-extremality parameter is nonzero.

Can the invariant matching construction extend to N=2 theories whose special Kähler moduli spaces lack a homogeneous-coset description? The paper limits its explicit treatment to models with tractable invariant data.

The radial-coordinate convention determines which direction a monotone flow runs and how extremal and non-extremal horizons are approached. The parameter c separates zero-temperature extremality from the non-extremal discussion.

Could singularities generated by perturbative gravitational graph sums encode the nonperturbative light states expected in a string-theory decoupling limit? The proposed connection is intended to bear on whether N=8 supergravity can stand as a complete quantum gravity.

Can perturbatively finite four-dimensional N=8 supergravity admit a nonperturbative completion and reproduce the light-state phenomena associated with a string-theory decoupling limit? Regge trajectories and cuts are investigated as possible perturbative clues rather than a resolution.
Can supersymmetric orientifolds coexist with dynamic SU(3)×SU(3) structures, and under what conditions do supersymmetry and form-field identities imply the source-corrected supergravity equations?

Isolate the effects of curvature and a cosmological horizon on vacuum decay while suppressing the response of the metric. A positive common vacuum-energy scale fixes Λ, while the much smaller variation of V supplies the transition barrier.

Determine a decay rate and post-transition initial conditions from a thermal scalar theory confined to a de Sitter causal diamond. The central issue is whether the usual Euclidean prescription requires information outside the observer's horizon.
Does the charge-return bound have an entropy interpretation, connect to the cited hep-th/0601001 arguments, or explain a Planck–GUT hierarchy in string constructions with many states?
Can a TeV sector with roughly 10³² species, or an admissible cyclic charge capacity of comparable size, account for the gravitational hierarchy?
Can many Standard Model singlets have natural portal strengths while retaining a charge realization compatible with the black-hole hierarchy argument?
Can the charge-return argument survive if massive species decay, provided their lifetimes exceed the relevant black-hole evaporation time?
Can an exactly conserved charge have unlimited range if it creates no classical long-range field and returning it through available carriers has a nonzero energy cost?
How much exactly conserved charge can a black hole store when each of N equal-mass species carries its own independent binary charge?

Can a large number of quantum-field species force gravity to be weak relative to their mass scale, thereby explaining the weak–Planck hierarchy and the Higgs mass's sensitivity to a much larger cutoff?
Can the rigid limit of an N=2 gauge theory embedded in supergravity reveal a new ultraviolet scale proportional to the gauge coupling times the Planck mass?
How does a gauge theory separate from gravity when an ADE singularity develops inside a compact K3-fibered Calabi–Yau threefold?
Can the holomorphic scale analysis be reconciled with gravitational corrections to gauge running and extended to N=1 theories produced by flux or brane deformations?

Can landscape inflation evade the small-tensor conclusion by using a different mechanism? The paper identifies successive vacuum tunnelling as an alternative outside its slow-roll field-budget calculation.
Can many identical scalar fields permit slow roll when a constituent potential is too steep? On the equal-field assisted trajectory, the Hubble slow-roll parameter is reduced by the number of fields.

Can a Wilson-line scalar acquire a large canonical normalization scale through a small four-dimensional gauge coupling? The extranatural-inflation example makes this possibility explicit before gravitational consistency restrictions are applied.

Can a scalar drive inflation through a canonical field excursion exceeding the Planck scale while remaining in the string landscape? The paper proposes a negative answer and tests selected constructions.

Does quartic inflation retain an effective-theory hierarchy between the Hubble scale and a gravitationally restricted ultraviolet cutoff? The paper asks this for both a pure quartic potential and a nonnegative constant added to it.

How does the canonical inflaton trajectory determine the inflationary expansion? The paper uses a spatially flat homogeneous background and counts e-folds backward from the end of inflation, with a monotonic field trajectory.

How should an initial thermal fermion state be propagated through a time-dependent electric background, and how does the produced current alter that background? Both questions require ingredients beyond the fixed-background bosonic occupation calculation.

How does a prescribed electric pulse change the pair occupation of an initially thermal charged-scalar ensemble? The relevant comparison is the excess late-time occupation over the initial population, with the electric field driving the state out of equilibrium.

Strong-field experiments and compact-star environments motivate studying pair creation from nonzero initial temperature. The source particularly discusses electron–positron production near hypothetical strange-star electrospheres.

A smooth electric pulse supplies a finite-time preparation and scattering problem while retaining analytic solvability. Initial and final frequencies differ because the gauge potential approaches different constants.

Can the excess occupation during the pulse be read as a number of already created particles? The source answers conditionally: a particle interpretation requires an approximately adiabatic positive-frequency basis.

The setting isolates pair creation by a classical electromagnetic background in a complex scalar field. Time dependence enters through the gauge potential, making even this quadratic matter theory a nonequilibrium problem.
Do nongeometric fluxes possess source solitons analogous to NS5 and KK5 objects, and can their contributions relax the corresponding flux constraints? The paper poses this as an unresolved extension.

Which flux and localized-source combinations define consistent compactifications and effective theories when geometrical flux changes the internal topology? The paper studies this question classically, principally for type-IIA orientifolds with four-dimensional supersymmetry.

Can KK5 orientations and localized magnetic flux generate useful D-term interactions or supersymmetry breaking? How do the resulting source-inclusive compactifications fit into existing gauged-supergravity and generalized-geometry classifications?
Why did a consistent N = 4 gauged-supergravity truncation with a supersymmetric AdS4 vacuum lack a ten-dimensional interpretation using only conventional fluxes and D6/O6 sources?
Which heavy-threshold interactions dominate Higgs observables when the new sector is approximately supersymmetric? The answer depends jointly on the heavy-scale ratios and η = cot β.
What is the constrained scalar-Higgs baseline against which new interactions are compared? Once v is fixed, the tree-level MSSM spectrum depends on mA and tan β.

Can discrepancies between measured Higgs masses and MSSM predictions, after determining the stop sector, reveal heavy additional degrees of freedom? Correlated Higgs and electroweakino observables provide further tests of the proposed effective interactions.
Can a broken additional gauge interaction provide Higgs quartic corrections while its vector multiplet is integrated out?
Can flux stabilization admit finitely separated vacua for identical fluxes, and can nonperturbative corrections produce a large-volume nonsupersymmetric de Sitter minimum without an anti-D3 uplift?
For extremal black holes, can one determine charges from prescribed attractor moduli and construct distinct superpotentials yielding the same black-hole potential?

Does network scaling extend to loop production, and is its small-scale cutoff set by gravity or microscopic thickness? Finite dynamic range and unresolved disagreement between Nambu and field-theory simulations prevent a controlled quantitative answer.

How reliably can observations identify cosmic strings and determine their properties when loop formation sizes are poorly known? The paper treats the macroscopic network-to-observation problem, with particular emphasis on gravitational radiation.

The model isolates uncertainties in string-network evolution by restricting the microscopic possibilities to one stable, purely gravitational string species. The dimensionless tension Gµ controls its gravitational strength.
Can warped flux backgrounds be described by four-dimensional supersymmetry data without first identifying a reliable finite set of light fields?

How can supersymmetric Euclidean D-branes be described using the spinor data of a Minkowskian flux background? The continuation must distinguish independent Euclidean chiralities while preserving the intended supersymmetry-component count.
Which ten-dimensional equations are retained, assumed, or lost when the generalized functional is restricted to conventional Calabi–Yau light modes?

How is a generalized flux compactification projected to the desired N=1 field content? The orientifold combines a world-sheet operation with an internal involution, with spinorial consistency determining whether a left-moving fermion-parity factor is needed.

Which supersymmetry-breaking contributions can cancel a small negative vacuum energy without overwhelming the non-perturbatively generated gravitino scale? The source explores existing uplift proposals and their compatibility with flux-stabilized sectors.

Can realistic anomaly-free brane sectors be built without destabilizing closed fields needed for anomaly-canceling axions? Can explicit geometries, twisted-sector alternatives, or brane networks realize the effective constructions?

Can non-geometric fluxes generate an exponentially small gravitino mass while retaining a high string scale and stabilizing all moduli, by first constructing perturbative W=0 Minkowski vacua and then introducing small non-perturbative effects?
Can a non-geometric flux sector generate the small constants needed by an ISS supersymmetry-breaking sector while stabilizing its gauge-coupling modulus perturbatively?
Can non-geometric type-II flux compactifications stabilize closed-string moduli at high scales while allowing an exponentially smaller gravitino mass and a compatible brane sector?
How can a flux compactification retain a brane anomaly-canceling axion while stabilizing the remaining fields and generating a small superpotential without a small perturbative constant?

The geometry separates a potentially GUT-sized SO(4) plane from four smaller compact dimensions. This permits an intermediate six-dimensional description with locally unified boundary symmetry and a smaller four-dimensional gauge group.

Can an anisotropic heterotic compactification produce a locally unified intermediate theory with consistent anomalies, three chiral families, and removable exotic matter? The further vacuum question is whether its singlet backgrounds and large dimensions can preserve supersymmetry and be stabilized.
Can local FI sources and the full supergravity fields support an N = 1 background with two dimensions much larger than the string scale? Can an isotropic supersymmetric vacuum be obtained as a limit?

How do the local matter spectra and Abelian charge conventions enter the bulk and fixed-point anomaly tests of this heterotic model? The supplied window distinguishes bulk and local gauge factors but leaves the compactification geometry and full gauge embedding to earlier pages.

Can the effects assigned to Dark Energy arise from averaging ordinary inhomogeneous matter and geometry in Einstein gravity? The question includes whether an FLRW prior changes the interpretation of observations taken on different scales and at different epochs.

Can curvature evolution link the onset of significant effective Dark Energy to the epoch of structure formation? The report identifies curvature–fluctuation feedback as the mechanism that fixed-background treatments suppress.

The setting isolates geometrical effects of averaging ordinary gravitating matter. It removes local pressure and rotational support so that positive regional acceleration, if obtained with zero cosmological constant, must come from the averaging terms.

Does an inhomogeneous universe evolve on average like an FLRW solution, and can structure-induced backreaction explain apparent Dark Energy within classical general relativity? This status report reviews the mechanism and strategies for establishing its quantitative and observational relevance.
How can a local Standard Model brane construction be embedded in a compact, globally consistent string background?
Can black-hole entropy supply a relative weighting of flux vacua beyond counting solutions?
Can entropy of domain walls associated with four-dimensional AdS flux vacua define a landscape probability functional?

String model building must connect moduli-dependent parameters to particle physics and cosmology. Flat moduli prevent definite coupling predictions, while their stabilization must remain within the regime of the effective description.
How can fluxes stabilize compactification parameters when the displayed superpotential omits Kähler moduli?
Can a large ensemble of string solutions yield useful distributions of particle-physics properties or a statistical account of a small cosmological constant?
How do compactification geometry and discrete string data produce the Standard Model, determine its couplings, and constrain the string and supersymmetry-breaking scales?
Can an independently stabilized, heavier modulus prevent the large relative X displacement induced by a modulus-dependent uplifting tadpole?
This family tests whether an instanton-dependent supersymmetry-breaking tadpole can coexist with stabilization of the same modulus controlling the instanton.
The effective theory isolates the light modulus whose stabilization and supersymmetry-breaking response can change when an uplifting field couples to it.
Does direct nonperturbative coupling between a supersymmetry-breaking field and a Kähler modulus preserve F-term uplifting and the suppressed modulus F-term characteristic of KKLT-type models?

Can multi-throat constructions with the same class of brane-motion corrections ease the duration and spectral difficulties, and can they transfer the inflationary energy into a successful reheating phase?

Can radial D3-brane motion, coupled to a stabilized but evolving volume modulus, yield enough inflation and acceptable primordial spectra? The relevant tests are inflation duration, scalar amplitude, scalar tilt, and tensor amplitude within the model and observational conventions supplied by the paper.
The compactification setting asks how the position of a mobile D3-brane and the overall volume evolve together during inflation, after flux stabilization of other closed-string moduli.

Do complex Euclidean wormholes exist in compactified supergravity, and can string theory include their saddle-point contributions? The paper distinguishes the classical existence problem from the compatibility of a complex integration contour with discrete gauge symmetry.

The classical existence problem is posed for scalar fields in Type II toroidal compactifications. Their noncompact symmetric target supplies many Killing directions, allowing the paper to compare different analytic continuations of the same positive-definite scalar theory.

Can covering-space supergravity saddles be interpreted in a string theory whose scalar space is an arithmetic quotient? The paper uses exact discrete gauge symmetry, rather than the broken continuous classical isometry, as the constraint on such an interpretation.

The desired solution joins two flat asymptotic regions through a nonzero spherical throat. In the displayed scalar-gravity equations, this geometry requires a negative scalar geodesic norm, which real profiles on the original Riemannian target cannot supply.

Can self-reproduction occur in the simple massive or quartic regimes of an assisted chaotic potential? The two contributions share a common field amplitude and total Hubble friction, but the conjectured cutoff remains tied to the quartic coupling.

Can quantum fluctuations sustain self-reproduction in an assisted chaotic inflation model while the effective inflaton theory obeys a conjectured gravitational ultraviolet cutoff? The question concerns slow-roll eternal inflation rather than persistent expansion of metastable vacua.

Can many identical scalar fields collectively sustain inflation when an individual field would roll too rapidly? Each field contributes to the common Hubble friction, while its potential derivative remains that of its own uncoupled potential.

Can observations discriminate cosmological theories through how typical those observations are, even when many different data sets exist? The paper locates the disagreement in the definition and normalization of likelihoods rather than in Bayes' theorem.

How can certain existence of two kinds of data coexist with strongly unequal observational probabilities? The toy model fixes unequal multiplicities and separately assumes equal weight per observer region.

Can a shorter theory description compensate for assigning less than unit probability to complicated observed data? The example models complexity by a large data-rank integer and compares theories within a shared ordering.

What counts as one possible observation must be fixed before comparing cosmological likelihoods. Perceptions, scientific records, planets, and causal pasts are alternative choices of observational description, with different contents and possible overlap.
Can perturbative type II compactifications produce supersymmetric AdS4 extrema with finite main moduli, and can their sources form domain walls connecting an AdS4 region to flat spacetime?
How does retained field content affect perturbative IIA stabilization with RR zero- and four-form fluxes and NS three-form flux, without metric flux?
Can brane degrees of freedom define an entropy for AdS4 flux vacua that matches a macroscopic thermodynamic quantity?
Do supersymmetric AdS4 domain walls possess attractor equations fixing horizon scalars independently of suitable asymptotic data?

Can physically realizable evolution form acoustic closed causal curves outside the backgrounds covered by temporal-function proofs? The paper invokes quantum backreaction by analogy with gravitational chronology protection.

How do scalar perturbations on a prescribed expanding background compare with perturbations that include the gravitational response of a scalar-driven universe? The comparison uses conformal time, a homogeneous background field, and distinct test-field and cosmological canonical variables.
Can a regular positive-kinetic background evolve through the NEC boundary? The proposed obstruction is quantum excitation near singular acoustic geometry, extending earlier cosmological arguments.

How does a response retarded in the acoustic medium's preferred time appear to a spacecraft moving with respect to that medium? The calculation uses a constant sound speed in three spatial dimensions and a coordinate Lorentz boost with gravitational invariant speed c.

Why can a stable acoustic wave equation appear unstable when data are specified at constant spacecraft coordinate time? The setting separates gravitational Lorentz coordinates from the acoustic cone selected by a timelike background.

Does a growing Fourier solution in moving coordinates demonstrate instability of the preferred-frame retarded response? The appendix compares kernels constructed with two different definitions of retardation and finds that they agree only on the slow branch.

Can a Lorentz-invariant nonlinear scalar theory have background-dependent signal cones without inevitable causal inconsistency? The distinction is between the symmetry of the action and the preferred frame selected by a scalar configuration.

Which combinations of quantum corrections and additional sources can stabilize Kähler moduli while preserving a controlled large-volume expansion? The appendix compares mechanisms by their competing potential terms, flux-superpotential magnitude, topology, and gauge-sector assumptions.

How can an internal volume become very large while one four-cycle remains comparatively small? This example separates the growing cycle \(\tau_5\) from the smaller cycle \(\tau_4\) through a difference of their three-halves powers.

Which cycle can support the nonperturbative contribution used to stabilize a small modulus inside a much larger compactification? The source selects a rigid blow-up cycle resolving a point-like singularity and distinguishes this requirement from the unfluxed instanton eligibility statement.

How do quantum corrections lift the tree-level Kähler-modulus flat directions of type IIB flux compactifications? The effective description separates flux-sensitive axio-dilaton and complex-structure fields from cycle-volume moduli whose perturbative dynamics arise through the Kähler potential.

When can string-loop corrections be neglected in moduli stabilization? The survey distinguishes corrections that bound a mechanism's validity from corrections that generate its stabilizing potential, and it warns that conclusions drawn from a few-modulus model need not survive additional flat directions.
What explains inflationary initial conditions, protects potential flatness, transfers energy into the hot Big Bang, and defines predictions across differently evolving causally separated regions?
What minimal field dynamics can keep the universe approximately vacuum dominated and later allow the field to evolve away?
Can one scalar sustain a nearly constant vacuum energy while a second scalar supplies an instability that ends inflation?

How should Lorentzian AdS/CFT accommodate tunable boundary sources and the normalizable modes required for Hamiltonian quantization, and how much local bulk dynamics can its boundary generating functional describe?
Can the free chiral two-form of the M5-brane admit an SL(6,Z)-invariant partition function on T^6, despite the difficulty of constructing a manifestly covariant six-dimensional Lagrangian?
How should the holographic entropy bound be formulated in cosmology, and what conditional restrictions would it impose on expansion, the equation of state, and spatial curvature?

For CFTs described by the conjectured AdS/CFT correspondence, how does the effective action depend on the chosen representative of the boundary conformal metric, and what Weyl anomaly follows from covariantly regularizing the bulk gravitational action?

Can supersymmetry-breaking modifications of perturbative Type IIB orientifolds produce anomaly-free, nonchiral and chiral large-N gauge theories with cancelled massless and tachyonic tadpoles, and inherit correlation-function reduction to a parent N=4 theory?

Can representation theory determine supergravity Kaluza–Klein spectra on S³×AdS3 and explain agreement with boundary CFT chiral primaries and the additional states required by the elliptic genus? The paper also investigates less supersymmetric six- and five-dimensional examples.
What are the timelike T-duals of Type II string theories, and can their E-branes and supersymmetric de Sitter backgrounds motivate large-N Euclidean gauge/string dualities and topological twists?

How can eleven-dimensional supergravity and electrically charged membranes and dyonic five-branes be described as a closed dynamical system, and how can a duality-symmetric formulation yield a five-brane coupling involving only the standard three-form potential?

Can the full Cremmer–Julia symmetries be generated from internal coordinate transformations in the eleven-dimensional and type IIB reduction pictures, intertwined by T-duality, and how does this explain duality identifications of torus geometry?
Can a string vacuum with supersymmetry broken at the string scale have vanishing perturbative cosmological constant, and can the cancellation extend beyond the first two loops?

Which rank assignments make finite-string-coupling brane box models consistent, and how do string consistency conditions distinguish worldvolume gauge anomalies from scale anomalies and NS5-brane bending?

Within semiclassical Type IIB string theory, do spacetime topology changes occur, which topologies should be summed, and do D-instanton wormholes induce third quantization or probabilistically distributed coupling parameters of the Coleman type?

To what extent can local bulk string and supergravity dynamics be recovered from CFT operators, particularly beyond the free large-N limit, and what can this description say about black-hole infall, complementarity, and the BTZ singularity?

What type IIB orientifolds are T-dual to elliptic type IIA configurations with O6-planes, especially oppositely charged pairs, and how do twisted tadpole conditions encode four-dimensional N=2 finiteness?

Can string constructions realize pure supergravity spectra with very few noncompact moduli, and can some resulting vacua remain disconnected from higher-dimensional geometric compactifications even at strong coupling?

Can inverse mean curvature flow extend mass and horizon-area bounds to asymptotically AdS black holes with nontrivial topology and to gravity with scalar/vector matter, thereby extending charge-dependent attractor bounds beyond static spherical solutions?

Can the protected topological A-model amplitudes of type IIA on a Calabi–Yau threefold be understood through a one-loop M-theory calculation, including constant maps, spherical bubbling and information beyond the graviphoton expansion?

Can Born–Infeld theory on a noncommutative two-torus describe compactified D-brane dynamics with T-duality acting on fluctuations as well as global charges, and how can its extra parameter θ be related to the string B-field modulus?

Does the two-loop cosmological constant still vanish in two special nonsupersymmetric type II models once coincident picture-changing-operator singularities and potentially finite collision terms are included?

Can supersymmetry breaking away from the visible brane naturally suppress flavor-dependent soft terms while unavoidable anomaly-mediated contributions generate viable, predictive gaugino and scalar masses?

How much of conjectured M-theory/heterotic duality can be exhibited through classical Kaluza–Klein reductions, including scalar cosets, field couplings, charge lattices and Yang–Mills-supported branes?
Can brane–antibrane creation and tachyon condensation explain why conserved D-brane charges belong to spacetime K-theory, including torsion charges of nonsupersymmetric Type I objects?
Can supersymmetry-breaking relevant deformations of known holographic CFTs reach new interacting infrared CFTs, and which candidate AdS endpoints survive classical stability tests?
Does the ’t Hooft expansion of SU(N) Chern–Simons theory on S3 equal a closed topological string on the resolved conifold, and can worldsheet dynamics explain the emergence of open-string boundaries?

How can the conformal theory on N D3-branes at a conifold be derived from an intersecting-brane construction, and how do its geometry, global symmetries and coupling moduli appear after lifting to M-theory?
Can counting holomorphic gauge invariants with Molien functions provide useful information about N=1 gauge theories and duality, particularly when global symmetries give limited constraints?

Which critical points occur in a particular SU(2)-invariant sector of five-dimensional gauged N=8 supergravity, and what supersymmetry, stability, central charges and ten-dimensional interpretations do their proposed conformal phases have?

Which near-horizon limits define AdS2 quantum gravity, which excitations and fragmented geometries survive, and can their ground states account for extremal black-hole entropy? When can charged-brane instantons fragment AdS universes?
What precise BPS information about wrapped M2-branes is encoded by Calabi–Yau threefold topological-string amplitudes, and how does dependence on the string coupling record five-dimensional spin?

Can the low-unification-scale TSSM protect proton stability and small neutrino masses through anomaly-free gauge symmetries, while preserving its unification prediction and yielding distinctive phenomenology?
Can singular Joyce orbifolds geometrically engineer four-dimensional N=1 pure Yang–Mills theories, and can fractional membrane instantons account for their superpotential and chiral anomaly?
Can the proposed nonperturbative IIB quotient construct the SO(32) heterotic string, explain its gauge sector through NS 9-branes, and describe what happens to world-sheet charges at finite coupling?
How can the symmetry Lie superalgebras of supersymmetric AdS × X backgrounds be identified geometrically, including cases where explicit Killing spinors are unavailable?

Can anomaly-free flavor gauge symmetries suppress FCNCs in the low-string-scale TSSM while preserving its proton-stability and neutrino-mass protections, particularly with two large transverse dimensions?

Can the ordinary S-matrix of an interacting massless scalar theory in five-dimensional Minkowski spacetime be recovered from timelike-boundary data of a bulk AdS theory in the flat-space limit? The paper emphasizes that the answer depends on what bulk quantization is intended.

Does the nonsupersymmetric gauge theory on self-dual Type 0 D3-branes inherit all-orders planar finiteness from N = 4 super-Yang–Mills, despite retaining SO(6) global symmetry? The paper also identifies a further SO(6)-invariant central orbifold.

How can one define a finite boundary stress tensor and conserved gravitational charges for asymptotically locally AdS spacetimes without requiring a reference-space embedding, while recovering stress-tensor properties expected from the proposed dual CFT?

Does the simple global structure of classical de Sitter space survive black-hole nucleation and quantum radiation, and what would fragmentation of future infinity imply for proposed holographic surfaces?
Can explicit analytic supergravity solutions describe one BPS brane localized at another, while retaining relative-position parameters useful for proposed bulk/boundary correspondences?
How should local mirror invariants of surfaces inside Calabi–Yau threefolds be defined, calculated in A- and B-models, and interpreted enumeratively, including suitable singular surfaces?
Can lifting infinite-N flat directions preserve an interacting nonsupersymmetric three-dimensional fixed point at large finite N, and what statement of IR duality survives?

What happens to the D1/D5 boundary CFT when mutually BPS subsystems can separate at zero energy cost, and can long-string dynamics explain its continuum, singular behavior, and apparently missing chiral primaries?

How can boundary SYM encode distant bulk collisions before their signals reach the boundary, while its stress tensor subsequently exhibits apparently instantaneous redistribution, superluminal oscillations and negative local energy?

Can a supersymmetric nonconformal gauge-theory flow have an explicit, controlled supergravity description, a detailed infrared operator map, and a monotonic holographic function interpolating between fixed-point anomaly coefficients?
When are RR tadpole cancellation and gauge anomaly cancellation equivalent in compact D=4,6 Type IIB orientifolds, and do tadpole conditions uniquely determine the gauge group?

Can nonquadratic scalar kinetic terms, without a potential, generate expanding Einstein-frame inflation with decreasing curvature, acceptable scalar perturbations and a graceful transition to a radiation-dominated universe?

Can an intrinsic boundary counterterm prescription assign finite energy, angular momentum and entropy to rotating four-dimensional Kerr–NUT/bolt geometries, including AdS and asymptotically locally flat cases, without reference-background subtraction?

How do linear quantum cosmological perturbations generalize to a scalar Lagrangian p(X,ϕ), and what scalar and tensor spectra distinguish slow-roll or power-law k-inflation from potential-driven inflation?

Does torus T-duality survive nonperturbative string-coupling corrections in heterotic compactification on K3×T², and what geometric or supersymmetry conditions support a physically meaningful duality group?

What motivates the holographic correspondence between large-N field theories and string/M theory on AdS backgrounds, what evidence tests it, and what can classical or semiclassical gravity calculate about strongly coupled field theories?

Which massless spectra, anomaly cancellations and R-R tadpole conditions make ten-dimensional D9–anti-D9 systems consistent, and does a symplectic orientifold projection yield a tachyon-free nonsupersymmetric USp(32) endpoint?
Can Bekenstein’s entropy/area bound be extended covariantly to strongly gravitating and cosmological regions by selecting suitable null hypersurfaces instead of arbitrary spatial interiors?

Can a covariant, background-independent holographic principle identify screens storing the information of general spacetimes, and what do their geometry and changing area imply for possible holographic theories?

Can local mirror symmetry compute higher-genus topological-string amplitudes for curves supported on Fano surfaces, reproduce localization invariants, and organize them into integral BPS coefficients with interpretable large-degree growth?
Can gravity appear four-dimensional with an infinite extra dimension and no Kaluza-Klein mass gap, through localization in a nonfactorizable background?
Which vacua, BPS domain walls, effective superpotentials, and infrared conformal theories arise near isolated Calabi-Yau four-fold singularities once flux and space-filling brane data are specified?
Can competing strong gauge dynamics stabilize a modulus at weak, unified gauge coupling while generating a hierarchy and retaining calculable low-energy quantities?
Can Hawking emission be derived directly as horizon tunneling while enforcing energy conservation, and how does the resulting emission law depart from thermality?

Can a global, time-symmetric modification of the Fischler–Susskind bound become viable and stringent in four-dimensional cosmologies with zero cosmological constant by counting history-compatible states rather than instantaneous entropy?
When is the Type II worldsheet path integral globally well-defined with boundaries on D-branes, and what global interpretation of the brane A-field and bulk B-field cancels the fermionic anomaly?

Can linear-dilaton holography describe six-dimensional heterotic little string theories, reproduce their known chiral operators, and generate additional theories through modular invariants and orbifolds?

Can a perturbative orientifold localize string-scale supersymmetry breaking on selected branes while keeping the bulk and other brane sectors supersymmetric at lowest order, with a chiral tachyon-free explicit example?
How can background G-flux produce supersymmetric warped M/F-theory vacua, cancel tadpoles, constrain moduli, and yield orientifold descriptions and heterotic compactifications with torsion?

Determine the moduli space and charged spectrum of the (4,0) CFT describing five-dimensional black strings, use them to obtain near-extremal four-dimensional black-hole entropy, and investigate a solvable CFT description.

Construct a nonabelian world-volume action for coincident Dp-branes compatible with T-duality, and determine how external fields can polarize branes into higher-dimensional noncommutative configurations.

How can causality and Poincaré covariance construct perturbative quantum gravity on flat spacetime, while operator gauge invariance controls interactions, physical graviton states and physical S-matrix unitarity?

Can small-instanton gauge sectors support four-dimensional gauge interactions while the heterotic string scale is arbitrarily low, in weakly and strongly coupled descriptions? What possible roles do these sectors have in supersymmetry breaking?

Can a universe brane moving through higher-dimensional bulk fields acquire an induced cosmology that resembles expansion driven by brane matter? How do world-volume energy and apparent initial singularities enter this description?
How can wrapped-M2 BPS spin data compute higher-genus topological strings, and what asymptotic constraints follow from spinning five-dimensional black holes?
What light BPS spectra occur under small deformations of Argyres–Douglas conformal points, and how do these spectra change with deformation direction?

Does the Fischler–Susskind (FS) entropy bound survive negative cosmological constant in (2+1)-dimensional cosmology, and which cosmological entropy bound is compatible with classical or quantum-modified generalized second laws (GSL)?

Which gaugings of five-dimensional N=2 Maxwell–Einstein supergravity remain supersymmetric when charged spectator vectors become tensor multiplets, and what restrictions follow for scalar potentials, AdS vacua, gauge groups and tensor representations?

How does circle compactification of quantum self-dual fields recover gravitational shifts in ordinary flux quantization: the Spin^c nature of a D4-brane gauge field from an M5-brane, and shifted Type IIA G₄ periods from the Type IIB self-dual G₅ field?

How strongly does topological censorship constrain the topology of Lorentzian asymptotically AdS interiors and black-hole exteriors from the topology of their timelike boundary, in arbitrary dimension and especially in 2+1 and 4+1 dimensions?
Can flux on a Calabi–Yau threefold realize the mass deformation that reduces a four-dimensional N=2 gauge theory to N=1, despite restrictions found for compact flux compactifications?

How should RR flux quantization be formulated when the fields are quantum mechanically self-dual and their topology is described by K-theory? The motivating difficulty is expressing the G₆ shift associated with a D-brane fermion global anomaly.
Does quantum matter on a classical collapse spacetime produce persistent black-hole emission, and what does that imply for temperature, horizon-area decrease, thermodynamics and evaporation?
Under what conditions can a black hole retain electric charge, and how can its spontaneous discharge through charged-particle production be calculated?
Is the original Kaluza–Klein vacuum classically and semiclassically stable, and how do energy positivity, allowed spacetime topologies, and elementary fermions affect that assessment?
Can separate scalar sectors suppress horizontal gauge exchange while retaining electroweak symmetry down to a lower scale and ultimately preserving electromagnetism?
Could the scalars responsible for horizontal and electroweak breaking arise from fermion bound states rather than require a separate unexplained scalar sector?
Can spontaneous breaking of a gauged family symmetry explain both very heavy right-handed neutrinos and much lighter left-handed neutrinos, with Majorana rather than purely Dirac masses?
The three-family extension places all displayed leptons in horizontal triplets so that family symmetry can organize neutrino and charged-lepton interactions within one gauge setting.
The reviewed models ask whether a local family symmetry can connect electronic and muonic matter while keeping induced flavour-changing interactions sufficiently weak.
How does gravitation alter semiclassical false-vacuum nucleation and subsequent bubble growth, and how does the change in vacuum energy alter spacetime inside and outside the bubble?

Do charged BPS-particle loops produce problematic extremal-black-hole entropy corrections even in N = 2 supergravity with nonminimal interactions, and can a magnetic weak-gravity cutoff or the string-theory interpretation of BPS states explain their avoidance?
How can the functional renormalisation group connect microscopic actions to macroscopic quantum physics, and provide evidence for a predictive, non-perturbative UV completion of gravity?

What do the electric and magnetic Weak Gravity Conjectures assert, what quantum-gravity motivations support them, and how are they refined for multiple gauge fields, massless scalars, extended charged objects, and broken supersymmetry?

Do Euclidean wormholes violate the global U(1) symmetry of a minimally coupled complex scalar theory in both its broken and unbroken phases, and how should their effects be matched onto local low-energy interactions when the wormhole action is infinite?

Can discrete symmetries in continuum low-energy theories have a local gauge origin, and can that origin enforce conservation and produce observable black-hole hair despite the absence of a low-energy gauge potential?

Can Euclidean wormholes exist without massless matter fields, and how do their charge, throat size, and effective operator insertions behave in a theory containing only a massive charged scalar and gravity?

What laboratory and astrophysical limits constrained neutrino electric charges, dipole moments and transition moments in 1999, especially for the small neutrino masses then favored? The review also derives a helioseismological constraint.

Which features of relativistic stellar collapse survive departures from spherical symmetry: horizons, singularities, a predictable exterior endpoint and extractable energy? Can collapse from reasonable nonsingular initial conditions instead produce a visible singularity?
Can a black hole assist a process that converts heat completely into work and thereby violates the second law?
The common geometric setting expresses horizon area and mechanical changes in terms of externally accessible mass, charge, and angular momentum.
What minimum information disappears from exterior access when a particle is swallowed, and can that minimum calibrate black-hole entropy?
Can a black hole serve as an entropy sink that converts all supplied heat into work through lowering and retrieval?
What uncertainty remains when exterior measurements specify a black hole's mass, charge, and angular momentum but cannot distinguish its internal configuration or formation history?
Can filtering maintain short wavelengths while making the radiation entropy per unit energy arbitrarily large?
Does adding an area-dependent black-hole entropy preserve a second-law inequality when ordinary entropy disappears through the horizon?
Can a candidate entropy functional survive a merger that loses information while radiating some of the initial energy?
Does capture of a maximum-entropy light beam preserve generalized entropy, and how do fluctuations limit such a test?
How can a second law remain meaningful for an exterior observer when a body carrying ordinary entropy disappears through a horizon?
How can black-hole area acquire the meaning and dimensions of entropy, and how should the second law account for ordinary entropy disappearing behind a horizon?

Are Wilson loops a complete family of continuous lattice-gauge observables? Equivalently, do conjugacy classes of every word in a finite tuple of group elements and their inverses determine its simultaneous conjugacy class?
For fixed Calabi–Yau X, count inequivalent supersymmetric flux vacua satisfying the tadpole constraint, determine their distribution in moduli space, and estimate the counting error as L→∞.

Determine canonical evaluations of κ_{g−2−i}λ_i in the tautological ring of smooth curves, organize them into logarithmic Hodge-integral series, and explain the associated polynomial identities combinatorially.

Give a mathematical proof of the anomaly-predicted relation between an elliptic Calabi–Yau threefold's Euler characteristic and gauge-group representations, and identify the accompanying geometric constraints under specified degeneration hypotheses.
Can compact 7-manifolds with holonomy exactly G2 be constructed by gluing asymptotically cylindrical SU(3) manifolds, and can Fano 3-folds supply matching building blocks?
Can monotone entropy quantities make Ricci flow gradient-like, prevent local collapse, and control singularity models sufficiently to advance Hamilton's geometrization program?

How can higher-dimensional quadratic refinements acquire geometry analogous to Riemann's theta functions and determinant lines, and what differential cohomological language supports their construction and fivebrane application?
How can geometric constructions with bundle gerbes clarify Deligne cohomology, holonomy, transgression and reconstruction, and describe classical topological actions?

The physical motivation is a previously derived asymptotic flux-vacuum counting formula involving a Weil-Petersson curvature integral. Its finiteness implications retain caveats from the cited counting work.
Are integrals of Weil-Petersson curvature invariants finite and rational on noncompact moduli spaces of polarized Calabi-Yau manifolds?

What are the connection, curvature, geodesics, exponential mapping and Jacobi fields of the infinite-dimensional manifold of Riemannian metrics with its canonical weak integral metric, including when the underlying manifold is noncompact?

Introduce the classification of rational CFT partition functions and explain Monstrous Moonshine through modular functions, representations, vertex operator algebras and generalised Kac–Moody algebras. These are pedagogical lectures reviewing existing developments.
How do lattice Z_N gauge theories realize Kitaev-type quantum memory, and how do electric fluctuations and static versus time-dependent random gauge couplings affect its stability?

How can the group structure of stabilizer codes support quantum error correction, efficient encoding, fault-tolerant computation, and bounds on code efficiency and channel capacity? The thesis combines an overview with constructions and calculations.

Can two-dimensional systems with local interactions protect quantum information physically and implement fault-tolerant computation through anyon braiding and fusion, without requiring an exact microscopic symmetry?

What upper limits do quantum mechanics, thermodynamics, relativity, and gravity place on computation speed, memory, and serial versus parallel operation? The benchmark is an ideal one-kilogram computer occupying one liter.
